deep.reconstruction:
Setting (§§15–17): steady flow from a vessel through a curved tube of variable cross-section zz into air through an orifice of area bb. The exit velocity corresponds to the head v, so the exit speed is √v. Coordinates are x = AP (vertical, downward) and y = PM (horizontal). Arc length is s, and Φ is the angle of the tube element with the vertical. Continuity gives the speed in section MN as u = b²√v/z². Euler's units make gravity 1 and speed² = head, so a force equals 2·(acceleration).

This page:
(i) The required accelerating forces are 2 d²x/dt² and 2 d²y/dt², with dt constant.
(ii) With dx/dt = u cosΦ and dy/dt = u sinΦ, differentiate using du = −2b²√v dz/z³:
d(dx/dt) = −u sinΦ dΦ − (2b²√v cosΦ/z³) dz,
d(dy/dt) = u cosΦ dΦ − (2b²√v sinΦ/z³) dz.
(iii) Multiply by 2/dt = 2u/ds to get the force components:
vertical: b⁴v(−2 sinΦ dΦ/(z⁴ds) − 4 cosΦ dz/(z⁵ds)),
horizontal: b⁴v(2 cosΦ dΦ/(z⁴ds) − 4 sinΦ dz/(z⁵ds)).
(iv) Rotate to intrinsic (tube-tangent and normal) axes:
tangential force = −4b⁴v dz/(z⁵ds) = d(u²)/ds, i.e. 2u du/ds in Euler's scaling;
normal force = −2b⁴v dΦ/(z⁴ds) = −2u² dΦ/ds, which is twice the centripetal acceleration u²κ in these units.
(v) Only the tangential component is needed. It must equal the actual driving force along the tube: gravity contributes cosΦ (§19), and a pressure difference begins in §20. The next page adds −dp/ds and the friction term −αp/z. This yields the linear ODE dp + αp ds/z = dx + 4b⁴v dz/z⁵, solved with the integrating factor e^{α∫ds/z}.

Purpose: a one-dimensional (hydraulic) momentum balance along a curved pipe with friction. It is used to compute how much friction reduces the efflux velocity below the Torricelli value.
errors: No mathematical errors: all differentiations, the multiplication by 2/dt = 2u/ds and the rotation to tangential/normal components check out.

Modelling gap: the normal (centrifugal) component is computed and then discarded. The implied transverse pressure gradient across a curved tube is not used, which is acceptable in a one-dimensional hydraulic model.
The friction law used next (resistance ∝ pressure p rather than velocity) is physically dubious by modern standards; this is not an error on this page itself.

ideas.what: Decomposing the acceleration of steady flow along a curved tube into tangential (u du/ds) and normal (u² dΦ/ds) parts.
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic (Frenet/natural-coordinate) decomposition of acceleration; convective acceleration in streamline coordinates
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (natural-coordinate dynamics, Mechanica 1736) and Euler's hydrodynamics 1750s
ideas.where_published: Mechanica (E15/E16); Principes généraux du mouvement des fluides (E226); also this paper E260

ideas.what: Continuity in a tube of variable section (u ∝ 1/area) combined with a tangential momentum balance of gravity, pressure gradient and friction.
ideas.modern_name: One-dimensional pipe-flow (hydraulic) momentum equation / generalized Bernoulli with head loss
ideas.usually_credited_to: Daniel Bernoulli (Hydrodynamica 1738), Euler; friction forms later by Chézy, Darcy, Weisbach
ideas.where_published: E260; related to Euler's E206/E258 on fluid motion through tubes

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine kinematic computation within a known paper (E260, discussed by Truesdell in the Opera omnia II.12/13 introductions). It contains a correct intrinsic decomposition of acceleration and nothing novel or uncredited.
